passes.evidence: Full pass over the extended-command prompt, which fired the commands gate at 1,289 of 1,000 unreviewed lines. Four finders ran; performance and concurrency were not enabled. 19 raw findings, 16 after deduplication, all 16 confirmed and none rejected. Four are applied at 2640c9f: three production defects and the generated-table test that pins the restored column. Twelve are deferred, and three of those are one defect seen from three angles — the port's flush_screen() is a whole-screen rebuild where display.c's re-emits only dirty cells, so the faithful vpline() flush_screen(1) call this range added erases an open tty menu at the two pre-existing menu-search call sites. .agents/review.md puts that outside audit-fix scope, because it changes rendering behavior and needs the gnew dirty discipline and gb.bot_disabled, which the port lacks; it is recorded in ROADMAP.md with the instruction to implement it and then run a new full pass over the expanded range rather than a delta. This pass does not cover that implementation. The applied fixes: tty_get_ext_cmd() had dropped C's iflags.extmenu guard entirely and the option was parsed and discarded, so a path meant to fail closed gave the typed prompt; a 0xFF byte was stored as text where C's signed char cast makes it EOF and cancels the line; and the generated table had dropped extcmdlist[]'s f_text column, which rhack() reads to name a counted command's occupation. Validation at 2640c9f: 1,808 tests passing, five generated-data checks including check:extcmds, check:namespace-members, development unchanged at 398 screens and 99,496 PRNG values, and the matrix matching 71,359 calls with 370 screens plus 12,261 calls with 33 screens in debug mode.

productionDefects.summary: tty_get_ext_cmd() dropped C's first statement, `if (iflags.extmenu) return extcmd_via_menu();`, replacing it with a comment. Nothing read the option at all: parseNethackrc accepted `extmenu` and discarded it, so a deliberately unported path did not fail closed and silently gave the typed prompt instead.

A 0xFF input byte was stored as ordinary text. cmd.c:452 ends pgetchar() with `return (char) ch;` and char is signed, so 255 arrives as -1 and getline.c:85 treats it as EOF, cancelling the line and setting iflags.term_gone. The restart arm is gated on Escape alone, so EOF cancels even over existing text.

The generated extcmdlist[] table dropped the sixth column, f_text, which rhack() reads at cmd.c:3728 to name the occupation a counted command starts. 'search' and 'wait' are the two rows carrying one, and neither the file nor the generator said a column was missing.

hooked_tty_getlin()'s new flush_screen(1) erases an open tty menu, because the port's flush_screen() is a whole-screen rebuild through _buildScreenOutput() while display.c's re-emits only dirty glyph-buffer cells and select_menu() sets gb.bot_disabled. The call itself is faithful to pline.c vpline(); the function it calls is not.
The two pre-existing ttyGetlinSearch menu call sites now run the new unconditional flush_screen(1) and are untested against the menu erasure it causes.

hooked_tty_getlin() ports pline.c vpline()'s `if (u.ux) flush_screen(...)` without the `state === game` guard that the other port of the same C line carries, so a non-global state would flush the wrong game.

Five finders including performance, enabled because the cloned scan now owns a terrain grid and vision buffers and the preflight re-derives the transparency index every elapsed turn; the performance finder confirmed nothing. 14 raw findings, 11 after deduplication, 10 confirmed, 2 applied at d7dd150, 8 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 1 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. The material defect was at the seam the pass was pointed at: the transparency-index restore was not side-effect-free, because recalc_block_point() runs rebuildVisionPoint(), which sets vision_full_recalc whenever the change touches the hero's current vision — the normal case for a door in a lit room — so the dry run left a flag the live scan then consumed as a vision_recalc(0) C never performs. The checked-in fixture could not show it, since its viz_array entry at the door is zero and rebuildVisionPoint() takes the other branch; the new test clears the squares between hero and door and recomputes first. The second applied finding is the orchestrator's own from the previous cycle: the trap guard reinstated at monmove.c:1509's position had no test, so deleting it left the whole suite green and the repaired defect could return silently. Of the eight deferred, four are comments that outlived the code they describe — including two that still describe the design the implementer abandoned when a focused test disproved it — and three are gaps in the isolation's own coverage. Development score identical before and after at 452 of 7,765 screens, 452 cursors and 99,971 PRNG calls; both door matrices match, 8 segments with 22,622 calls and 248 screens, and 6 segments with 17,436 calls and 146 screens.

passes.evidence: Full /audit-diff-correctness pass over the monster-door goal's last slice, the hero's two diagonal doorway refusals. Four mandatory finders; performance and concurrency not triggered. 17 raw findings, 12 after deduplication, 10 confirmed, 2 applied at 3471a99, 8 deferred to ROADMAP.md, 2 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. The pass caught a regression the slice introduced, and it is this goal's failure mode for the seventh time: a silent divergence rather than a stop. preflightDomoveDestination() short-circuited on refusedDiagonalDoorway() before its destination-monster branch, inverting domove_core()'s order, so a monster diagonally adjacent to a hero on an intact doorway was admitted and then refused inside test_move() instead of raising 'hero combat or displacement' — the port never attacked where C attacks, and with mention_walls on printed a line C never prints. The comment licensing the short-circuit stated the false rule outright. No existing case covered it: the one monster case the slice added uses a tame pet, which C also refuses, and every direct test_move() test clears the monster grid first. The fix restores C's order and adds a hostile-on-the-diagonal case that fails when the short-circuit is reinstated. Development score identical before and after at 459 of 7,765 screens, 459 cursors and 99,980 PRNG calls; the diagonal doorway matrix matches 14 segments, 35,931 PRNG calls and 38 screens.

passes.head: 3471a99a07b6fb35dbb8a2d63801ee4c787a380a
passes.evidence: Light delta review of the movement-seam ordering fix, run because the monster-door goal's holdout evaluation is a review deadline and audit-fix debt cannot stand across one. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace); readability is the perspective a light pass drops. 8 raw findings, 6 after deduplication, 6 confirmed and all 6 applied at ff865ec, none deferred, none rejected, none unverified, no warnings. This is the fourth consecutive goal in which a delta review found collateral from the previous fix, and this time it found the fix wrong in two ways. Half of it was dead: the refusal guard added for the safemon path was the last statement of its block with nothing after the chain, so deleting it changed no test, while its comment asserted an invariant that did not hold. And moving the pet-swap seam ahead of the refusal made the port throw a segment-ending boundary for a trap or object on the pet's square, on a step C declines without consulting them. The adjudicator settled the question the finder left open by going to the C: uhitm.c:474 evaluates foo = (Punished || !rn2(7) || ...) inside do_attack()'s is_safemon branch, so C spends a draw even for the pet before returning FALSE and letting test_move() refuse — which means neither the original nor the first-fix ordering matched C, and admitting the step silently diverges by exactly one rn2(7). Any monster on a refused diagonal now fails closed, safemon included, ahead of the swap-consequence gates. The pet test asserted the silent refusal and now asserts the boundary plus an unchanged draw count, since failing closed means before the draw rather than instead of it. Development score identical before and after at 459 of 7,765 screens, 459 cursors and 99,980 PRNG calls; the diagonal doorway matrix matches 14 segments, 35,931 calls and 38 screens.

productionDefects.summary: Moving requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap() ahead of the diagonal refusal made the seam throw a boundary for a trap, floor object, region or engraving on the pet's square, on a step C refuses inside test_move() without ever consulting them — reintroducing on the monster arm the hazard already recorded for the empty-square arm.

The refusal guard added for the safemon path was the last statement of the destination-monster block with nothing after the else-if chain, so it had no effect and deleting it changed no test, while its comment asserted that the diagonal refusal claims the step exactly as on an empty square. The adjudicator settled the underlying question: uhitm.c:474 evaluates foo = (Punished || !rn2(7) || ...) inside do_attack()'s is_safemon branch, so C spends a draw even for a pet before returning FALSE and letting test_move() refuse, and admitting the step silently diverges by exactly that rn2(7).

passes.head: ff865ec919042f747f12d44962b8c7b2f782bc2a
passes.evidence: Second light delta review in the chain repairing the movement seam, run because the monster-door goal's holdout is a review deadline. Three finders (correctness, tests, variable-trace). 10 raw findings, 8 after deduplication, 6 confirmed and all 6 applied at 278bf6c, none deferred, 2 rejected, none unverified, no warnings. Both production findings are against the orchestrator's own previous commit, and the first is a claim that should have been checked before it was written: the comment justifying the fail-closed throw asserted the port has no do_attack() and cannot spend uhitm.c:474's rn2(7) until combat lands, when do_attack() is ported at js/uhitm.js:51 with that draw at :70 and domove() calls it live at :1098 — an ordinary pet swap draws it today. That is the third comment in this chain to assert an invariant the tree does not have. The throw remains load-bearing for a different reason, now stated: domove() runs test_move() at :1065 before the do_attack() call, the reverse of hack.c:2794 and :2841, so admitting the step refuses it inside test_move() and never reaches the draw, and the removal condition is a domove() reorder rather than a trigger that has already fired. The second finding is that the ordering half was pinned by nothing — swapping the throw back after requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap() left the suite green, because the pet fixture's square holds nothing and every swap gate returns. A trap on the destination distinguishes them and now reports 'pet swap trap interaction' under the base order, a boundary naming a situation C never reaches. Development score identical before and after at 459 of 7,765 screens, 459 cursors and 99,980 PRNG calls.

productionDefects.summary: The justification for the new fail-closed throw was factually wrong: it claimed the port has no do_attack() and cannot spend uhitm.c:474's rn2(7) until combat lands. do_attack() is ported at js/uhitm.js:51 with the draw at :70, and domove() calls it live at :1098, so an ordinary pet swap draws it today. The throw is still load-bearing, but because domove() runs test_move() at :1065 before that call — the reverse of hack.c:2794 and :2841 — so admitting the step refuses it inside test_move() and never reaches the draw. A maintainer greping for do_attack would have read the stated removal condition as already met and deleted the guard.

The half of the change placing the refusal ahead of requireOrdinaryStartingPetSwap() was pinned by no test: swapping the two statements back left the whole suite green, because the pet fixture's square holds no trap, object, region or engraving and every swap gate returns.
